angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 374,982 km at 35.65 pc = 0.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 28.0525 +/- 0.0242 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 35.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.539 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Wilson et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LHS 1903 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026Sci...392l2348W/abstract): 374,982 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.538 +/- 0.039 solar masses from Wilson et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LHS 1903 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026Sci...392l2348W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3664 +/- 70 K from Wilson et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1903 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026Sci...392l2348W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Wilson et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1903 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026Sci...392l2348W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lhs-1903.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.706, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
